title: Previous-Column Anchor and Offset Geometry Controls First-Row Gap Records
novelty_claim: The live novelty claim is that boundedness or unboundedness is governed by an endogenous paired-mex backbone: the previous-column term sits inside each late row-gap interval and the offset Delta_n = T(n,1) - T(1,n) may control how the skipped block splits around that anchor. This is a T-specific geometric state variable, not a reformulation of generic multiplication-table coverage.
closest_prior_art: OEIS A129258, OEIS A129259, Kimberling's problem page, with Ford's multiplication-table and divisor-in-an-interval work as the nearest overlap branch to clear.
differentiation: This direction survives only if anchor position, left/right subinterval lengths, and Delta_n predict late record formation better than generic local product density or prime-placement summaries. Composite-only record gaps are the guardrail: the mechanism must work with no skipped primes at all.
easiest_falsifier: Matched non-record windows or axis-swapped late records show that anchor and offset observables are no more discriminative than window size alone, or the previous-column anchor consistently certifies only one skipped value and does not control interval-scale coverage.
evidence_plan: On one independently checked baseline run, export every late record gap together with matched non-record windows. For each window, log the previous-column anchor location, Delta_n, left/right interval lengths, skipped-prime flags, and a minimal witness summary; then compare those observables against matched surrogate product-window controls before allowing any theorem-style language.
budget_envelope: Champion lane. One bounded corpus-refresh pass plus one falsifier control pass. No outward literature expansion unless the final writeup needs exact Ford-clearance on divisor-interval language.

title: Frontier Witness Hypergraphs Stay Forest-Like at Late Gaps
novelty_claim: The strongest remaining rescue route for witness-based structure is not compact chosen-witness certificates but a full-hypergraph invariant: late frontier witness graphs may stay acyclic or uniformly low-cycle-rank, so long gaps arise from larger tree-like components rather than denser local rectangle structure.
closest_prior_art: Ford-style product-coverage literature is still the overlap risk, with sparse bipartite or C4-free graph theory only as comparison language rather than provenance.
differentiation: This lane is viable only if the forest-like profile persists under full witness export, survives witness-canonicalization changes, and beats matched non-record and surrogate product-window controls. If the same profile is generic, the claim collapses back into the falsified strong-H1 story.
easiest_falsifier: The first persistent positive cycle-rank frontier window, frequent C4 rectangles near late records, or surrogate windows reproducing the same arboricity and component profile at matched scale.
evidence_plan: Using the same verified corpus as H1, export full witness hypergraphs for late record gaps and matched non-record windows, then compute cycle rank, component sizes, diameters, leaf fraction, and arboricity under at least two witness canonicalizations and against surrogate controls.
budget_envelope: Backup lane. Activate only after the anchor/offset corpus exists. One structural audit pass; no extra horizon chase and no standalone graph-mining campaign.

title: Persistent Residue-Class Locking Creates Composite-Only Frontier Blocks
novelty_claim: A lower-overlap reserve hypothesis is that long row-1 gaps come from a small family of moduli whose row-border and column-border residue occupancies force long covered composite blocks before the next mex. That is an upstream obstruction story, not a prime-gap narrative and not an after-the-fact witness relabeling.
closest_prior_art: OEIS A129258, OEIS A129259, and Kimberling provide the object and question; there is no direct named overlap branch stronger than generic modular heuristics unless the claim drifts back into divisor-density language.
differentiation: This line survives only if one or two modulus families remain predictive across scales, matched controls, and at least one admissibility perturbation. Heatmaps or residue anecdotes do not count.
easiest_falsifier: No persistent modulus family survives window matching or a small admissibility perturbation, or any residue signal disappears once anchor position and window size are controlled for.
evidence_plan: Piggyback residue logging for small q on the same late-record and matched-window corpus used for H1 and H2. Promote this line only if the modulus features outperform the anchor/offset and witness-forest observables on held-out windows.
budget_envelope: Reserve lane. One cheap scan only if the champion and backup both fail to differentiate. No standalone modular exploration program.
